title: One line in, one line out
request: An application_data record whose plaintext is `hello\n` — six bytes inside the AEAD, plus the inner content type and the tag
response: An application_data record whose plaintext is `olleh\n`. The record on the wire is opaque; only the length gives its size away.
note: Compare the two record lengths in the hex: both are 6 + 1 + 16 = 23 bytes of ciphertext. The extra byte is the inner content_type and the 16 are the tag.

request_fields.value: 23 bytes: the AEAD ciphertext plus its 16-byte tag. The real content type is inside it, after the content and before the padding.

response_fields.value: 23 bytes: the AEAD ciphertext plus its 16-byte tag. The real content type is inside it, after the content and before the padding.

title: Exactly what `-rev` does
request: Read until a newline. Strip trailing CR and LF. Reverse the remaining bytes. Write them, then one LF.
response:
`hello
`   -> `olleh
`
`abc
`   -> `cba
`
`
`        -> `
`
`abc` (no newline) -> nothing, until a newline arrives
note: The reference reads into a fixed buffer, so a line longer than that buffer is answered in chunks, each reversed on its own. This suite keeps its lines well under that so the contract stays simple.
